message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s not done through the city council itself. Noise complaints are handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** (APD), which then may involve the city’s code enforcement or public works departments as needed.

### How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Contact Info |
|------|------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Call 911** if you’re in immediate danger or if the noise is part of a crime. | 911 |
| 2 | **Call the Atlanta Police Department non‑emergency line** for routine noise complaints. | 404‑656‑4000 |
| 3 | **Use the APD online reporting system** for convenience and to keep a record. | [Atlanta Police Online Reporting](https://www.atlantapolice.org/online-reporting) |
| 4 | **Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website** for additional resources on noise ordinances and public safety. | [City of Atlanta Official Site](https://www.atlanta.gov/) |

#### Quick Tips

- **Provide details**: When filing, give the exact address, time, and nature of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs).
- **Record the incident**: If possible, note the date, time, and any witnesses.
- **Follow up**: You can check the status of your complaint via the online portal or by calling the non‑emergency line.

### Why the City Council Isn’t the First Point of Contact

The **city council** in Atlanta is the legislative body that passes ordinances and budgets. While they set the rules (like the city’s noise ordinance), they don’t handle individual complaints. That responsibility falls to the police department and, if necessary, the city’s code enforcement office.

---

If you have any more questions—whether about the specific noise ordinance, how to appeal a decision, or other local regulations—feel free to ask!
